title: cross-run-history
description: The declaration of the harness-scoped logs under history_dir, and the whole of what decides which events reach them. One property per log, named for the file it declares, holding that log read as an array of parsed lines: its items.properties.event.enum enumerates the execution-history event kinds routed to that log, and its items.properties declare the fields a record there carries. Selection and record shape are therefore one file rather than a condition written into append_event, and adding a kind to a log is an edit here and nowhere else. The `event` property is the selection and is not itself projected: a record carries the other declared fields, so what routed it is read off the enum that named its kind rather than repeated on every line. A field the execution-history entry does not carry is omitted rather than written null, which is the rule execution-history.json already follows. A record is a summary and never a copy: the per-run artifacts hold the detail, and a log that duplicated them would inherit their size and lose its queryability. History is evidence, never state — nothing here is read back to make a routing decision, and the only read of a log at all is the prune that bounds it by history_retention_days. One further log is named here as RESERVED and is deliberately not declared above: adjudication-log.jsonl. This harness has no producer for it — adjudication is a level 4 concept it does not have — so it creates none, and naming it here rather than shipping an empty file is the whole of what it does about it. A later harness that acquires a producer declares its log as a property beside the ones above, and gets the projection with no change to orchestration — which is what inspection-log.jsonl, reserved here until this harness acquired the producer that writes it, now demonstrates rather than predicts. The per-log declarations are properties rather than a $defs block because the harness's own validator honors a deliberately small keyword subset and refuses a schema claiming a constraint it cannot check; a property named for its log carries the same declaration and stays checkable.

execution-log.jsonl.description: One record per point an execution reached, rather than one per execution that reached an outcome. Written to .harness/history/execution-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the point is reached rather than assembled as a terminal summary. A run that paused for capacity, was resumed and then completed therefore leaves three lines in that order, so a resumed execution is distinguishable in the record from an uninterrupted one — which is the whole reason a pause and a resume are recorded here at all: a pause carries its own exit code precisely so a caller can tell it from completion and from escalation, and an execution that reached one and left no line was indistinguishable in this log from one that never started.

event.description: The execution-history event kinds routed to this log. This enum is the selection and nothing else decides it: an entry whose kind appears here is projected into this log, and an entry whose kind appears in no log's enum is projected nowhere. The property is not projected into a record: it declares which kinds arrive here, not a field a line carries.

story_id.description: The story this execution ran, derived from the run directory's own name.

status.description: The point the execution reached, derived from the event kind that produced the record rather than threaded through the coordinator to serve this projection. Two of these values do not end an execution: capacity-paused says the run stopped to wait, and resumed says it continued, so a line carrying either is a point rather than an outcome.

retry_count.description: How many retries the execution took, counted from the retry decisions already present in the run's own execution history, which append_event has loaded to number the entry it is appending.

verifier_outcome.description: The verifier's verdict, when the entry that produced this record carried one. Absent otherwise.

timestamp.description: When the outcome occurred, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against.

inspection-log.jsonl.description: One record per inspection a completed run made of what its story changed. Written to .harness/history/inspection-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the inspection ends. It exists because the run directory is gitignored and reaches no clone: an inspection reporting only into that run's events.log would leave no evidence in the repository that any inspection had ever run. A record is a summary and never a copy — what was found, filed and dropped is here as three counts, and which finding went which way is in the run's own events.log and in the outbox entries the inspection wrote. The inspection is a total function that may not block, delay or refuse a run, so a record here is also what a configuration it could not obey is named in: an inspection that was not made because the file cap was unusable leaves a line saying so with its counts at zero, because naming the problem is the only thing a function that cannot refuse can do about it.

event.description: The execution-history event kinds routed to this log, on the terms the execution log's own event property states: this enum is the selection, and the property is not projected into a record. It names this kind alone, which is what keeps an inspection out of execution-log.jsonl, mandate-log.jsonl and retry-log.jsonl: none of their enums names it.

story_id.description: The story whose completed run made this inspection, derived from the run directory's own name.

timestamp.description: When the inspection ended, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against.

findings.description: How many findings the invocation produced. Present even where it is zero: an inspection that found nothing is an answer, and a line whose counts are all zero is how an inspection that was not made at all is distinguished from one nobody ran.

filed.description: How many of those findings reached the outbox as briefs.

dropped.description: How many were dropped, for every reason together. Which way each went is not summarised here: it is in the run's own events.log, where each reason is named with how many went that way.

mandate-log.jsonl.description: One record per mandate conferred: the harness-scoped record of an authorizing act, written by the process that observed it rather than by a run. Written to .harness/history/mandate-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the act is observed. It is the only declared log with no producer inside a run — no execution-history entry the coordinator appends carries this kind, so nothing a run does reaches it, and what does reach it is a caller outside a run using the same per-log append with an explicit history directory. That is the whole of what makes the conferring record a schema entry rather than a condition in orchestration: adding the kind here is what routes it, exactly as it is for the two logs beside this one. A record is a summary and never a copy: the block it records lives in the artifact it was appended to, and this line is what outlives the working tree that artifact was written in.

event.description: The event kinds routed to this log, on the terms the execution log's own event property states: this enum is the selection, and the property is not projected into a record.

story_id.description: The work item the mandate was conferred on.

timestamp.description: When the authorizing act was observed, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against, and it is the conferred_at the block itself carries.

conferred_by.description: The identity the act was observed from, as the block records it.

source_kind.description: The kind of source the block names, so a reader can tell what a run's resolution would have terminated at without opening the artifact.

recorded_by.description: The harness process that observed the act and wrote the block. Absent when the entry carried none.

discarded_session_block.description: Whether this conferral discarded a mandate block the planning session had written into the artifact. The observing process refuses such a block rather than trusting it, and the developer it asks is shown that the block is there and that approving discards it, so a true here records an approval given with that in front of them and a false records a conferral onto an artifact that carried none. It is written on every conferral rather than only on the true case, because a boolean has a false to say and absence would then mean either that or a record written before this field existed. A rejection writes no record at all — nothing was conferred, and this log holds conferrals — so a plan the developer declined leaves no line here, and that absence is the mechanism working rather than a gap in it.

retry-log.jsonl.description: One record per retry a story's execution took. Written to .harness/history/retry-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the retry is routed.

event.description: The execution-history event kinds routed to this log, on the terms the execution log's own event property states: this enum is the selection, and the property is not projected into a record.

story_id.description: The story whose execution took this retry, derived from the run directory's own name.

timestamp.description: When the retry was routed, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against.

stage.description: The stage the entry belongs to. Absent when the entry carried none.

retry_decision.description: The routing decision the entry recorded. Absent when the entry carried none.

retry_category.description: The retry category the verifier reported, as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. Absent on a retry that carries no category.

retry_stage.description: The stage the retry was routed to. On a self-routed entry it names the entry's own stage, because a self-route has no destination other than itself.
